heuristics: H1: coordinates of a random GT element behave as independent uniform values (low-bit index and distinguished-point fields are then independent, statistical distance 2^-175 over all steps), and the class-level r-adding walk with a 2^16-entry table behaves like a random mapping on the N' Frobenius classes up to the additive-walk penalty sqrt(1+1/R) (van Oorschot-Wiener 1999, Teske 2001, Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe 2011, Bos et al. 2010, Duursma-Gaudry-Morain 1999); an explicit extra margin factor 1.20 on steps is charged, and success 0.39 holds up to a 1.44 times larger effective collision space.

H2: fruitless cycles of the class map have rate exactly 1/(12R) for length 2 and at most B_L = sum_b C(R,b)(b/R)^L 12^-b for every L >= 3 (a table index in a cycle must occur at least twice); cycles of length <= 24 are detected by a class-defined rule (revisit of a label within 24 steps, escape by squaring the member with the smallest label) and charged (2^-17.263 of the steps); longer cycles are bounded for every length (at most 2^-190.2 per class, waste 2^-61.6 of the steps) and by the closure term (trapped trails 2^-65.4, under one step).
limitations: Peak memory 2^74 bytes (stored distinguished points, theta = 2^-60, 80-byte records at hash load 1/2, plus 2^20 per-processor tables) is not physically realisable; it is declared, and has no scalar cost.

Not a practical attack and not a claim of novelty; the per-step overhead is a charged bound (8000 instructions against 4466 itemised), not a measured count, and the 1.20 step margin and 1.07 reserve are explicit and not derived.

The toy experiment (60013-element group, pseudorandom stand-in for the coordinate) measures the walk's steps-to-collision at 1.04 times the random-draw value (95% interval up to 1.07) and is evidence only at that scope.
